key_insight: Two geometric multigrid preconditioner families deliver robust iteration counts for aggregation-stabilised unfitted finite element discretisations of the de Rham complex.
engineering_relevance: These solvers support efficient simulation on meshes that need not conform to complex boundaries, with applications to scalar and vector PDEs.
method: Apply multigrid directly to unfitted operators using background mesh hierarchies and aggregation-aware star-patch smoothers.
Combine cut-cell patch smoothing with an auxiliary body-fitted problem solved by non-nested geometric multigrid.
Use both approaches in block-diagonal preconditioners for mixed Hodge Laplacians.
evidence_signal: Experiments in 2D and 3D report iteration counts robust to cut configuration, mesh size and level count, with additional tests of higher order, weak Dirichlet conditions and face-based stabilisation.
watch_item: Implementation requires carefully designed patch smoothers and mesh hierarchies; robust iteration counts alone do not establish low setup cost or wall-clock scalability.
paper_title: Geometric multigrid preconditioners for unfitted discretisations of the de Rham complex
